liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Althea** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Jerry flubs some lyrics, a minor slip; the jam is packed with strong Jerry leads; The Althea gap is about two minutes missing, with a 3-4 second hole; the text understates it [2][27][28]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): The Scarlet into Fire transition is called especially stellar; Scarlet into Fire on the Mountain is described as flawless [26][29][34]
- **Walking The Dog** (2 reviews): Singled out as a rare song to hear in this show; Reviewer is a fan of the Walkin' The Dog opener on the setlist [26][36]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Bird Song and Looks Like Rain in the first set especially hooked the reviewer [34]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Estimated Prophet is played with strong conviction [29]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drums go down to primal beats that had the crowd howling with joy [29]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-11-11.143073.sbd.cole.miller.tobin.pp.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 143 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1985-11-11.mtx.seamons.95966.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 144 min; rated 3.85/5 by 13 [2]
- **gd1985-11-11.143076.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 143 min [3]
- **gd1985-11-11.143075.dts.tobin.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 143 min [4]
- **gd85-11-11.naks.cohen.17960.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 145 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [7]. Said about its sound: Taper's recording has a solid, rumbling bottom end, said to outdo the Oade brothers' work; Audience recording has heavy, full low end that makes speaker cabinets rumble [30][36]
- **gd85-11-11.aud.oade.19303.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 143 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [8]
- **gd1985-11-11.fob.senn441.mccue.LMPP.94621.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 146 min; rated 4.67/5 by 6 [11]. Said about its sound: Recording is snappy and in-your-face, bringing the show vividly back [35]
- **gd85-11-11.sbd.doughty.14862.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 136 min; rated 3.8/5 by 10 [14]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sound is described as superb [34]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended as a band guest; at night's end Dan Healy handed over the soundboard master cassettes to the group [25]
- This was the reviewer's first Dead show, launching three years of nonstop touring [26]
- Weir is very loud in the mix and seems to be enjoying himself [27]
- Reviewer attended this as their third or fourth show while in high school [32]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-11-11.143073.sbd.cole.miller.tobin.pp.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller and Kevin Tobin and Matt Cole; source: Remastered & Patched & Pitch Corrected Soundboard - SBD:(original shnid = 14862) Lineage: SBD>CM>DAT>DAT>CD>EAC>SHN>WAV>CE2K>shntool>mkwACT(seekable) Editing:… [1]. Also: Soundboard patched and pitch-corrected, mixed by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in September 2018 [1]
- **gd1985-11-11.mtx.seamons.95966.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [2]. Also: Schoeps CMC441 mics, front of board, 90 degrees, 17cm, into Oade M118 and modified Sony PCM-F1; then DAT and DAW [2]
- **gd1985-11-11.143076.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: flac16/48kHz ; 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound (48k) - SBD (shnid = 14862) [3]. Also: 5.1 LPCM surround mix at 48k made in Adobe Audition CC 2014, converted to FLAC in September 2018 [3]
- **gd1985-11-11.143075.dts.tobin.flac1644**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: DTS-Audio-CD 5.1 Mix; - SBD (shnid = 14862) [4]. Also: DTS surround mix by an archive.org user, FLAC converted in September 2018, meant for burning to a regular audio CD [4]
- **gd85-11-11.naks.cohen.17960.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Mark Cohen; transferred by Anne Cohen.; source: Audience analog cassette master 2 Nakamichi cm-700's > Sony tc-d5M(dolby b) [7]
- **gd85-11-11.aud.oade.19303.sbeok.shnf**: source: Schoeps CMC441 (FOB, 90deg, 17cm) > Oade M118 > Oade modSONY PCM-F1 [8]. Also: Speed of this audience recording differs greatly from the soundboard's speed [28]
- **gd1985-11-11.fob.senn441.mccue.LMPP.94621.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Mark McCue; transferred by Alex Ford; source: (FOB) 2 x Sennheiser 441 > Sony D5 > Maxell XLII-S 90(Set I) and TDK MA-R90(Set II). Mic Config: forehead level, PAS. Location: FOB, 26th row, ROC [11]
- **gd85-11-11.sbd.doughty.14862.sbeok.shnf**: source: Lineage:SBD>CM>DAT>DAT>CD>EAC>SHN>WAV>CE2K>shntool>mkwACT(seekable)Editing: SHN>WAV>CE2K> shntool>mkwACT Transfer by Ken Doughty. Editing by Matt Cole. Seeded… [14]. Also: The cassettes given out were Maxell XLII tapes, which the reviewer later lost around 1989 in college [25]

claims.text: Reviewer attended as a band guest; at night's end Dan Healy handed over the soundboard master cassettes to the group
The cassettes given out were Maxell XLII tapes, which the reviewer later lost around 1989 in college
Singled out as a rare song to hear in this show
The Scarlet into Fire transition is called especially stellar
This was the reviewer's first Dead show, launching three years of nonstop touring
Jerry flubs some lyrics, a minor slip; the jam is packed with strong Jerry leads
Weir is very loud in the mix and seems to be enjoying himself
The Althea gap is about two minutes missing, with a 3-4 second hole; the text understates it
Speed of this audience recording differs greatly from the soundboard's speed
Scarlet into Fire on the Mountain is described as flawless
Estimated Prophet is played with strong conviction
Drums go down to primal beats that had the crowd howling with joy
Taper's recording has a solid, rumbling bottom end, said to outdo the Oade brothers' work
Reviewer attended this as their third or fourth show while in high school
Bird Song and Looks Like Rain in the first set especially hooked the reviewer
Scarlet>Fire and Estimated>Eyes get praised as great versions; the set fades after drums and space
Soundboard sound is described as superb
Recording is snappy and in-your-face, bringing the show vividly back
Audience recording has heavy, full low end that makes speaker cabinets rumble
Reviewer is a fan of the Walkin' The Dog opener on the setlist
Schoeps CMC441 mics, front of board, 90 degrees, 17cm, into Oade M118 and modified Sony PCM-F1; then DAT and DAW
A gap about 54 seconds into disc 1 track 4 for Althea; notes say 3-4 seconds, but about two minutes are missing
Soundboard patched and pitch-corrected, mixed by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in September 2018
5.1 LPCM surround mix at 48k made in Adobe Audition CC 2014, converted to FLAC in September 2018
DTS surround mix by an archive.org user, FLAC converted in September 2018, meant for burning to a regular audio CD
